reason: The English terminal sentence grammatically merges two clinical questions ("what complication" and "which cue to prioritize") via "and" into one sentence, while the Chinese segmentation splits the same two questions across the penultimate sentence ("基于新的临床表现，最可能出现的新发并发症是什么？") and the terminal sentence. Per spec §9.3, EN/ZH sentence counts need not match; here both languages ask the identical two questions with no content added, omitted, or contradicted — a segmentation difference, not a bilingual defect.

terminalSentenceEn: (Drag the steps into the correct sequence.)
terminalSentenceZh: 拖动步骤以排出正确的顺序）
quotedEvidence: (Drag the steps into the correct sequence.)
reason: Standard ordered-response demand phrased as a parenthetical instruction. Zh terminal retains only the closing full-width paren "）" while the opening "（" attaches to the Zh penultimate sentence, because Intl.Segmenter splits the parenthetical clause at the full-width open-paren boundary; the En terminal keeps the whole "(...)" together as one sentence. This is the same benign segmentation-artifact family as the recurring "（多选）"/"（多项选择）" case (e.g., queueIndex 1858, 2370), just with more retained content — the full underlying Zh stem reads coherently and the learner never sees the per-sentence split.
